name: Sports & Games
description: From football to chess, challenge yourself with athletic and strategy trivia across 11 levels.

questions.question: How many players are on the field for one team during a regulation football (soccer) match?
questions.explanation: A team consists of 11 players including 1 goalkeeper on the field.

questions.question: Which country won the inaugural FIFA Men's World Cup in 1930?
questions.explanation: Uruguay hosted the tournament and defeated Argentina 4-2 in the final in Montevideo.

questions.question: How long is a standard professional football match excluding extra time and stoppage time?
questions.explanation: A match consists of two 45-minute halves totaling 90 minutes of regulation play.

questions.question: Which country has won the FIFA Men's World Cup the most times?
questions.explanation: Brazil has won the World Cup five times (1958, 1962, 1970, 1994, 2002).

questions.question: From what distance is a standard soccer penalty kick taken from the goal line?
questions.explanation: The penalty spot is precisely 12 yards (10.97 meters) from the center of the goal line.

questions.question: Who was the Brazilian football legend who won three FIFA World Cups (1958, 1962, 1970)?
questions.explanation: Pelé (Edson Arantes do Nascimento) is the only player in history to win three World Cups.

questions.question: Which club has won the UEFA Champions League / European Cup the most times?
questions.explanation: Real Madrid has won the European title a record 15 times.

questions.question: What color card does a referee show to immediately expel a player from a match?
questions.explanation: A red card results in the player being sent off and the team playing down a player.

questions.question: Which Argentine legend captained his nation to World Cup victory in Mexico 1986 and Qatar 2022 respectively?
options: Alfredo Di Stéfano and Juan Román Riquelme
questions.explanation: Maradona inspired Argentina in 1986, while Messi captained the triumph in Qatar 2022.

questions.question: What is it called when a single player scores three goals in a single football match?
questions.explanation: Scoring three goals in one game by an individual player is known as a hat-trick.

questions.question: How many legal deliveries are bowled in a single standard over in cricket?
questions.explanation: An over consists of six consecutive legal balls delivered by the same bowler.

questions.question: What is the exact length of a cricket pitch between the wickets?
questions.explanation: The cricket pitch is a rectangular area 22 yards (20.12 meters or 1 chain) long.

questions.question: Which Australian batsman finished his Test career with a legendary batting average of 99.94?
questions.explanation: Sir Donald Bradman's Test batting average of 99.94 remains one of sport's greatest statistical achievements.

questions.question: In what year was the first Men's Cricket World Cup (Prudential Cup) held in England?
questions.explanation: The West Indies won the inaugural World Cup at Lord's in London in 1975.

questions.question: What does the cricket umpiring abbreviation 'LBW' stand for?
questions.explanation: Leg Before Wicket occurs when the ball strikes the batsman's leg or pad preventing it from hitting the stumps.

questions.question: How many total players are on the field during play in cricket?
questions.explanation: There are 13 players on the field: 11 fielding team members plus 2 batsmen.

questions.question: Which bowler holds the world record for the most wickets taken in Test cricket (800 wickets)?
questions.explanation: Sri Lankan spin maestro Muttiah Muralitharan took 800 wickets in 133 Test matches.

questions.question: What is the famous biennial Test cricket series contested between England and Australia called?
questions.explanation: The Ashes urn originated in 1882 after a mock obituary stated English cricket had died at the Oval.

questions.question: What is it called when a batsman is dismissed on the very first ball they face?
questions.explanation: Getting out for zero on the first delivery faced is known as a golden duck.

questions.question: In standard T20 cricket, how many overs does each side bat for?
questions.explanation: Twenty20 cricket limits each team to a single innings of maximum 20 overs.

questions.question: In tennis scoring, what traditional term denotes a score of zero?
questions.explanation: Love is thought to originate from the French word 'l'oeuf' (the egg), resembling a zero.

questions.question: Which four tournaments comprise the tennis 'Grand Slam'?
options: Australian Open, French Open, Wimbledon, US Open
Wimbledon, Indian Wells, Miami Open, US Open
Davis Cup, ATP Finals, French Open, Wimbledon
Australian Open, Rome Masters, Wimbledon, US Open
questions.explanation: Winning all four major championships in a calendar year constitutes a Grand Slam.

questions.question: On what surface is the prestigious Wimbledon Championships played?
questions.explanation: Wimbledon is the only major tennis tournament played on natural grass courts.

questions.question: What score represents a tie at 40-40 in a tennis game?
questions.explanation: At deuce, a player must score two consecutive points (Advantage, then Game) to win.

questions.question: Who holds the all-time record for the most Men's Grand Slam singles titles in tennis?
questions.explanation: Novak Djokovic has won 24 Grand Slam singles titles.

questions.question: Which female tennis player won 23 Grand Slam singles titles in the Open Era?
questions.explanation: Serena Williams won 23 major singles titles between 1999 and 2017.

questions.question: What is the projectile used in the sport of badminton called?
questions.explanation: A shuttlecock has a cork base embedded with 16 overlapping goose or duck feathers.

questions.question: What is the maximum allowed number of bounces the ball can make on a side in table tennis before being struck?
questions.explanation: The ball must bounce exactly once on the receiver's court before being returned.

questions.question: What Grand Slam tournament is famously played on red clay at Roland-Garros in Paris?
questions.explanation: The French Open (Internationaux de France) is played on slow red clay courts.

questions.question: What is a tennis serve called that hits the court legally without the receiver touching it?
questions.explanation: An ace is a legal serve that touches inside the service box and isn't touched by the receiver.

questions.question: How many players from each team are on the court at one time in a basketball game?
questions.explanation: A standard basketball team plays with 5 players on the court (two guards, two forwards, one center).

questions.question: Who invented the game of basketball in Springfield, Massachusetts, in December 1891?
questions.explanation: Dr. James Naismith nailed peach baskets to the gymnasium balcony railings to create the sport.

questions.question: How many seconds does an NBA team have on the shot clock to attempt a field goal?
questions.explanation: The NBA introduced the 24-second shot clock in 1954 to speed up game pace.

questions.question: Which NBA superstar led the Chicago Bulls to six championships in the 1990s?
questions.explanation: Michael Jordan won six NBA Finals MVP awards with the Bulls (1991-1993, 1996-1998).

questions.question: How many points is a free throw worth in basketball?
questions.explanation: An uncontested free throw shot from behind the free-throw line awards 1 point.

questions.question: What is the height of a regulation basketball hoop rim above the gym floor?
questions.explanation: A regulation basketball rim is suspended exactly 10 feet (3.05 meters) above the court.

questions.question: Who holds the all-time scoring record in NBA history, surpassing Kareem Abdul-Jabbar in 2023?
questions.explanation: LeBron James broke the record on February 7, 2023, scoring over 40,000 career points.

questions.question: Which NBA player is celebrated as the greatest 3-point shooter in history, holding the all-time 3-point record?
questions.explanation: Steph Curry revolutionized the sport with his prolific three-point shooting for the Golden State Warriors.

questions.question: What is it called when a player records double digits in three statistical categories in a single game?
questions.explanation: A triple-double occurs when a player reaches 10+ in points, rebounds, and assists (or blocks/steals).

questions.question: How long is each quarter in a standard NBA game?
questions.explanation: An NBA game consists of four 12-minute quarters totaling 48 minutes (FIBA uses 10-minute quarters).

questions.question: In which country were the Ancient Olympic Games originally celebrated?
questions.explanation: The ancient games were held every four years in Olympia in honor of Zeus from 776 BCE.

questions.question: In which city were the first modern Olympic Games held in 1896?
questions.explanation: Pierre de Coubertin founded the IOC and revived the Olympic Games in Athens in April 1896.

questions.question: How many interlocking rings are featured on the official Olympic flag?
questions.explanation: The five interlocking rings (blue, yellow, black, green, red) represent the five inhabited continents.

questions.question: Who holds the all-time record for the most Olympic gold medals won by any athlete (23 golds)?
questions.explanation: American swimmer Michael Phelps won 23 gold medals (28 medals overall) across five Olympic Games.

questions.question: Which Jamaican sprinter set the world records in the 100m (9.58s) and 200m (19.19s)?
questions.explanation: Usain Bolt set both enduring sprint world records at the World Championships in Berlin in August 2009.

questions.question: How often are the Summer Olympic Games normally held?
questions.explanation: The Olympic Games are traditionally held every four years (an Olympiad).

questions.question: What Olympic symbol is lit in Olympia, Greece, and carried by relay to the host city?
questions.explanation: The Olympic flame is kindled by parabolic mirror at the Temple of Hera in Olympia.

questions.question: Which city has hosted the Summer Olympic Games three times (1908, 1948, 2012)?
questions.explanation: London was the first city to host the modern Summer Olympic Games three times.

questions.question: What sport features events like balance beam, uneven bars, vault, and floor exercise?
questions.explanation: Women's artistic gymnastics includes these four apparatus disciplines.

questions.question: In the ancient Olympics, what was the winner of an event crowned with?
questions.explanation: Victors at Olympia were crowned with an olive wreath (kotinos) cut from a sacred tree.

questions.question: How many total squares are on a standard tournament chessboard?
questions.explanation: A chessboard features an 8x8 grid of 64 alternating light and dark squares.

questions.question: What is the only chess piece that can jump over other pieces on the board?
questions.explanation: The Knight moves in an 'L' shape (two squares one way, then one square perpendicular) and can leap over pieces.

questions.question: Which piece in chess has the greatest freedom of movement, combining the powers of rook and bishop?
questions.explanation: The Queen can move any number of vacant squares in any direction: horizontal, vertical, or diagonal.

questions.question: What special move allows the King and a Rook to move simultaneously in chess?
questions.explanation: Castling helps safeguard the king while activating the rook into the center.

questions.question: What is the term for a situation in chess where a player's king is in check with no legal move to escape?
questions.explanation: Checkmate ends the game immediately as a win for the attacking player.

questions.question: What happens in chess if a player has no legal moves and their king is NOT in check?
questions.explanation: Stalemate occurs when the player to move has no legal move and is not in check, resulting in a draw.

questions.question: Who was the Russian grandmaster who held the World Chess Championship title from 1985 to 2000?
questions.explanation: Kasparov became the youngest undisputed World Champion in 1985 at age 22.

questions.question: Which Norwegian chess prodigy became World Chess Champion in 2013 and held the highest FIDE rating ever (2882)?
questions.explanation: Magnus Carlsen won five classical World Championships and reached a peak rating of 2882.

questions.question: What is the special pawn capture rule that translates from French as 'in passing'?
questions.explanation: En passant permits a pawn to capture an opponent's pawn that advanced two squares past it.

questions.question: What international governing body oversees world chess ratings and championships?
questions.explanation: FIDE (Fédération Internationale des Échecs) was founded in Paris in 1924.

questions.question: How many innings make up a standard professional Major League Baseball (MLB) game?
questions.explanation: A regulation baseball game consists of nine innings unless tied or shortened by weather.

questions.question: In American football, how many points is an uncontested touchdown worth?
questions.explanation: A touchdown is worth 6 points, followed by an extra point attempt (1 point kick) or 2-point conversion.

questions.question: How many players from each team are on the field at once in American football?
questions.explanation: Each side fields 11 players during an American football play.

questions.question: Which legendary New York Yankees slugger was known as 'The Sultan of Swat'?
questions.explanation: Babe Ruth hit 714 career home runs and transformed American baseball in the 1920s.

questions.question: What is the championship game of the National Football League (NFL) called?
questions.explanation: The Super Bowl is the annual championship game of the NFL, watched by over 100 million viewers.

questions.question: How many bases are there on a standard baseball diamond including home plate?
questions.explanation: The bases are First, Second, Third, and Home Plate, arranged in a 90-foot diamond.

questions.question: In American football, what position primarily receives the snap and passes or handoffs the ball?
questions.explanation: The quarterback is the offensive leader who orchestrates play calls and passes.

questions.question: What is it called when a baseball batter hits the ball over the outfield fence in fair territory?
questions.explanation: A home run allows the batter and all runners on base to score safely.

questions.question: How many strikes result in a strikeout for a batter in baseball?
questions.explanation: Three strikes result in a strikeout, retiring the batter.

questions.question: How many yards must an American football offense gain within four downs to earn a fresh set of downs?
questions.explanation: Gaining 10 yards earns a 'First Down' and restarts the 4-down counter.

questions.question: What prestigious Formula 1 street circuit race winds through the narrow streets of Monte Carlo?
questions.explanation: The Monaco Grand Prix has been held since 1929 and is part of the Triple Crown of Motorsport.

questions.question: Which British racing driver has won 7 Formula 1 World Drivers' Championships, tied with Michael Schumacher?
questions.explanation: Sir Lewis Hamilton won championships in 2008, 2014, 2015, 2017, 2018, 2019, and 2020.

questions.question: What famous 24-hour endurance sports car race is held annually near the town of Le Mans, France?
questions.explanation: The 24 Hours of Le Mans has tested mechanical reliability and driver endurance since 1923.

questions.question: What flag is waved at the finish line to signify the conclusion of an auto race?
questions.explanation: The black-and-white checkered flag signals that the winner has crossed the finish line.

questions.question: Which Italian racing team is the oldest surviving and most successful team in Formula 1 history?
questions.explanation: Ferrari has competed in every World Championship season since the inaugural 1950 championship.

questions.question: What famous American open-wheel automobile race is held annually at the Indianapolis Motor Speedway on Memorial Day weekend?
questions.explanation: The 'Indy 500' runs 200 laps over a 2.5-mile oval circuit, totaling 500 miles.

questions.question: In Formula 1, what does 'DRS' stand for?
questions.explanation: The Drag Reduction System opens a flap in the rear wing to reduce aerodynamic drag for overtaking.

questions.question: Who was the Brazilian Formula 1 triple World Champion beloved for his mastery in wet conditions?
questions.explanation: Ayrton Senna won world titles in 1988, 1990, and 1991 before his tragic crash at Imola in 1994.

questions.question: What is the top stock car racing series organization in the United States?
questions.explanation: The National Association for Stock Car Auto Racing (NASCAR) was founded by Bill France Sr. in 1948.

questions.question: What safety device made of titanium is mounted above the cockpit of modern F1 cars to protect the driver's head?
questions.explanation: The Halo was introduced in F1 in 2018 and has prevented serious head injuries in high-speed crashes.

questions.question: Who famously proclaimed 'Float like a butterfly, sting like a bee' and won the world heavyweight boxing championship three times?
questions.explanation: Muhammad Ali (Cassius Clay) was one of the most celebrated cultural and athletic figures of the 20th century.

questions.question: In which country did the martial art of Judo originate under founder Jigoro Kano?
questions.explanation: Jigoro Kano developed Judo in Japan in 1882 from traditional jujutsu schools.

questions.question: What is the maximum duration of a single round in professional men's boxing championship bouts?
questions.explanation: Professional championship boxing rounds last 3 minutes with 1-minute rest periods in between.

questions.question: In martial arts like Karate and Taekwondo, what color belt universally represents the highest standard student rank before master grades?
questions.explanation: A black belt signifies competent mastery of fundamental techniques and principles.

questions.question: What Korean martial art is known for its emphasis on head-height kicks, jumping spinning kicks, and fast kicking techniques?
questions.explanation: Taekwondo developed in Korea during the 1940s and became an official Olympic medal sport in 2000.

questions.question: What shape is the fenced fighting enclosure used by the Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC)?
questions.explanation: The trademarked UFC Octagon has eight padded sides enclosed by vinyl-coated chain-link fence.

questions.question: What is the traditional Japanese national sport of heavyweight wrestling called?
questions.explanation: Sumo wrestlers (rikishi) attempt to force opponents out of a circular ring (dohyo).

questions.question: What martial art known as 'The Art of Eight Limbs' utilizes punches, kicks, elbows, and knee strikes?
questions.explanation: Muay Thai is the national combat sport of Thailand utilizing eight points of contact.

questions.question: Which undefeated boxer retired with a perfect professional record of 50 wins and 0 losses?
questions.explanation: Mayweather retired with a 50-0 record across five weight classes.

questions.question: What Brazilian grappling martial art focuses on ground fighting and submission holds, developed by the Gracie family?
questions.explanation: BJJ emphasizes leverage and technique to enable smaller practitioners to submit larger opponents.

questions.question: What is the official distance of a standard athletic marathon race?
questions.explanation: The marathon distance was standardized at 42.195 km at the 1908 London Olympic Games.

questions.question: How many events are contested in a men's track and field decathlon?
questions.explanation: A decathlon comprises 10 track and field events held across two consecutive days.

questions.question: Which four strokes are contested in competitive swimming and the individual medley?
questions.explanation: The four competitive swimming strokes are butterfly, backstroke, breaststroke, and freestyle.

questions.question: What is the vulcanized rubber disc used in ice hockey instead of a ball called?
questions.explanation: An ice hockey puck is 1 inch thick, 3 inches in diameter, and weighs between 5.5 and 6 ounces.

questions.question: In the winter sport of curling, what are the heavy granite projectiles slid across the ice sheet called?
questions.explanation: Curling stones are crafted from rare water-resistant granite quarried on the Scottish island of Ailsa Craig.

questions.question: What is the length of an Olympic-sized swimming pool used for international competition?
questions.explanation: An Olympic pool is 50 meters long, typically 25 meters wide with 10 lanes.

questions.question: What track and field throwing event uses a spear-like metal implement?
questions.explanation: Athletes sprint along a runway before launching the javelin for maximum distance.

questions.question: In which country were the first Winter Olympic Games held in 1924?
questions.explanation: Chamonix hosted the inaugural Winter Olympics in January and February 1924.

questions.question: In golf, what term describes completing a hole in one stroke under par?
questions.explanation: A birdie is 1 stroke under par; an eagle is 2 strokes under par; a bogey is 1 over par.

questions.question: What sport combines cross-country skiing and rifle marksmanship in the Winter Olympics?
questions.explanation: Biathlon challenges athletes to maintain stamina during skiing while controlling heart rates for precision shooting.

questions.question: Who was the first human to officially run a mile in under four minutes in May 1954?
questions.explanation: Sir Roger Bannister ran the historic sub-4-minute mile (3:59.4) at Oxford on May 6, 1954.

questions.question: Which Romanian gymnast scored the first perfect 10.0 in Olympic gymnastics history at Montreal 1976?
questions.explanation: 14-year-old Nadia Comăneci was awarded seven perfect 10s at the 1976 Montreal Olympics.

questions.question: Which African-American track star won four gold medals at the 1936 Berlin Olympics in front of Adolf Hitler?
questions.explanation: Jesse Owens won the 100m, 200m, long jump, and 4x100m relay, defying Nazi racial propaganda.

questions.question: Who holds the record for the most total Olympic medals won by any gymnast (18 medals)?
questions.explanation: Soviet gymnast Larisa Latynina won 18 Olympic medals (9 gold, 5 silver, 4 bronze) between 1956 and 1964.

questions.question: Who scored 100 points in a single NBA basketball game in March 1962 for the Philadelphia Warriors?
questions.explanation: Wilt Chamberlain scored 100 points against the New York Knicks in Hershey, Pennsylvania.

questions.question: In what year did Kenya's Eliud Kipchoge run the first sub-two-hour marathon (1:59:40.2) in Vienna?
questions.explanation: Kipchoge broke the two-hour barrier in a specially orchestrated INEOS 1:59 Challenge in October 2019.

questions.question: Which golfer holds the record for winning 18 Men's Major Championships?
questions.explanation: Jack Nicklaus ('The Golden Bear') won 18 majors between 1962 and 1986.

questions.question: Who holds the record for the fastest goal in FIFA World Cup history (scored in 11 seconds in 2002)?
questions.explanation: Turkish striker Hakan Şükür scored against South Korea just 11 seconds after kickoff in 2002.

questions.question: Who was the first woman to officially complete the Boston Marathon with a bib in 1967 despite race officials trying to stop her?
questions.explanation: Kathrine Switzer finished the race with bib #261, breaking the barrier for women in distance running.

questions.question: Which boxer delivered the iconic 'Rumble in the Jungle' knockout of George Foreman in Zaire in 1974?
questions.explanation: Muhammad Ali employed the famous 'rope-a-dope' strategy to exhaust and defeat Foreman in Kinshasa.
